policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed, then decide using the updated crossings value and the cube motion in this step's frames: - Determine the cube's motion from the last two frames shown at this step, in this order. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in those two frames, it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as MOVING AWAY, whatever the distances are. (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each of the two frames. If it is decreasing, the cube is MOVING TOWARD the target. If it is equal, or increasing by only a small amount (fewer than about 5 px between the two frames, i.e. under about 1 px per timestep, which happens only at the far end of the swing where the cube is slowing to turn around), the cube is AT THE TURNAROUND, which counts as 'not moving away'. If it is increasing by more than that (the outward sweep after a crossing, where consecutive frames move about 7 px or more), it is MOVING AWAY. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is not moving away (moving toward the target, or stationary at the turnaround). No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is still moving away from the target (including the case where the (N-1)th crossing lies between the last two frames, so the cube is just passing the target and about to sweep outward). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is heading toward the target, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: cube_side
fields.description: The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. Overwrite it every step. e.g. larger_x
